summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma, ulcerative colitis, asthma, and a history of DVT/PE was admitted for her 18th cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She tolerated the treatment well with no significant side effects. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately, falling to 0.07 by discharge, with no renal toxicity. Liver enzymes showed mild, expected elevation. A brain MRI confirmed stable disease without lymphoma recurrence. Aspirin was held during admission to optimize methotrexate excretion and was restarted at discharge. She remained emotionally stable on citalopram with no depressive symptoms. Chronic right foot pain persisted and was managed with gabapentin and PRN oxycodone; she was advised to follow up with her primary care physician for further evaluation. She was discharged home in good condition with plans to start Rituxan in the upcoming cycle.
problems: Other malignant lymphomas, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
